hook: A U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command mission report (33 SOS, 27 SOW) documents an incidental UAP sighting at 0035Z on 27 October 2023 during an ISR/target development mission over the Aegean Sea, describing a seemingly circular object flying just above the ocean surface and executing multiple 90-degree turns at approximately 80 MPH before being lost from the sensor feed at 0038Z.
why_it_matters: This report is notable because it captures a UAP with sharp right-angle maneuvers from an AN/DAS-4 targeting pod aboard a special operations platform — a sensor suite optimized for precision tracking — yet the crew still lost the object within three minutes. The contradictory combination of anomalous kinematics (90-degree turns at 80 MPH) with a 'Benign' observer assessment and a determination that the object was 'not under intelligent control' illustrates the interpretive uncertainty embedded even in structured military reporting formats. The document was declassified in January 2026 and formally released to AARO, placing it within the current statutory UAP disclosure pipeline.

key_findings.finding: The UAP executed multiple sharp 90-degree turns at an estimated 80 MPH while flying just above the ocean surface, behaviors logged in a structured MISREP field as well as in the freetext narrative.

key_findings.finding: The observing crew described the UAP as seemingly circular but too small to resolve further detail, and the contact lasted only approximately three minutes from first sighting to loss of feed.

key_findings.finding: Despite logging anomalous 90-degree turns, the observer formally assessed the UAP as benign, not under intelligent control, and with no detected signatures across RF, physical effects, or equipment interference.

quotes.text: UAP Under Intelligent Control (yes/no; if yes, describe): NO

key_findings.finding: The reporting unit was 33 SOS (Special Operations Squadron) under 27 SOW and AFSOC/USCENTCOM, and the UAP observation was incidental — the primary mission was ISR target development for a violent extremist organization campaign.

quotes.text: Global Campaign Plan: GCP - VEO (violent extremist group)

key_findings.finding: The aircraft was equipped with an AN/DAS-4 targeting pod, AWGMESH, and Link 16 data link; full motion video was exploited by GET (Ground Exploitation Team), totaling 13 hours 30 minutes of mission time with 6 hours 29 minutes of FMV collection.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO 01/26/26' and the UAP event was submitted to AARO as a formal UAP incident report under USCENTCOM MDR 26-0019.
